- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to historical mean or recent peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.30), model underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to reflect risk aversion or market recovery bias.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp declines; apply a “rebound bias” correction: add 1–3% to early forecast values.
- After a price spike (e.g., >10% from 18-day mean), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 3–7% for the following 5 days.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: if model is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence; if below, add 1–3% per day.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with forecast error: when sentiment shifts sharply, model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period spikes (last 5–7 days); add a “late-period sensitivity” rule: if sentiment >0.60 in last 5 days, increase forecast by 1–4% for final 5 days.
